BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline points

1. **The "FINAL / settled at principal level / market standard" preamble has no authority.** Under playbook sec 0.4 and 6.3, a counterparty's statement that terms are agreed, final or market-standard does not make them so. We have no record of any principal-level agreement, and no written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback. We should treat every position as open and say so in our cover note. If anyone on our side had principal-level conversations, we should confirm that internally before responding. It does not change the drafting position.

2. **The draft is built to hollow out recovery in layers:**
   - a low cap;
   - high thresholds on an excess-only basis;
   - a short claims period;
   - title folded into the general regime;
   - limitations applied to "all Claims of any nature", which would capture fraud;
   - whole-data-room deemed disclosure;
   - a blanket constructive buyer-knowledge bar.

   Each layer is a problem alone. Together they could neutralise almost every claim, including the specific indemnities.

3. **The Seller's cover note contradicts its own Disclosure Letter.** The cover note says Bluefen is "addressed", the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" and DD-006 is "not expected to be material". The Disclosure Letter says there is no Bluefen consent, the bonuses are not in the funds flow, and the incident is unassessed. We should use the Disclosure Letter's facts, not the cover note's characterisations, and point out the inconsistency in negotiation.

4. **The facts are stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. The status of Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-006, Ironquay and Sandbar must be refreshed before we rely on any of it. That applies in both directions: we should not assume matters have worsened or been resolved.

---

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability architecture

| # | Seller position | Playbook | Departure and reasoning | Push-back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cap of 20% / AUD 4.8m (cl 12.1) | 25% / AUD 6m. 20% is a fallback **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft | The figure matching our fallback does **not** clear it (sec 6.3). No authority exists. Conceding now would also give away our fallback against a draft that is far off-side on everything else. | Counter at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not signal the fallback. |
| 2 | De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k, excess only (cl 12.2) | AUD 5k; AUD 50k; first-dollar recovery once exceeded | De minimis is 5x ours and the basket 5x ours. Excess-only permanently writes off AUD 250k of proven loss. The "~1% of price is market" claim is an unverified assertion. | AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping basket. |
| 3 | 18-month claims period (cl 12.3) | 24 months; 18 months needs Amelia Frost approval (none given) | Off-side, with no authority to move. | 24 months. |
| 4 | "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 13) | Categories kept separate; no hidden general-regime override | This default-rule drafting would silently apply general caps, thresholds and time limits to title, tax, IP, indemnities, payment obligations and covenants unless every one is carved out expressly. It is the classic hidden override. | Delete. Reverse the default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims unless expressly stated. |
| 5 | Title and capacity under general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Title is the core of what we are buying. Capping title at 20% means a total title failure recovers at most AUD 4.8m of AUD 24m. Administrative simplicity is not a reason to accept that. | Reject outright. Reinstate the fundamental regime. |
| 6 | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, to the maximum extent enforceable; **non-waivable** | As drafted, this purports to cap and time-bar fraud claims and to exclude reliance even where we were deliberately misled. Enforceability against fraud may be limited in any event, but we must not accept drafting that attempts it. No one on the team can concede this point. | Insert an express fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out overriding cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 and all of cl 12–13. Non-negotiable. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**7. General disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7).**
- The Seller deems disclosed everything in the data room as at 22 September 2026 (expressly including DD-002 to DD-012), plus the Accounts, the statutory registers and all publicly searchable records. This is exactly the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure the playbook rejects.
- Practical consequences:
  - Including DD-012 would arguably qualify the title warranty by reference to the Seller's own register.
  - Including DD-002 to DD-006 would arguably qualify warranties covering the very matters (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, the incident) for which we need protection.
- **Push-back:** delete 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure should be limited to specific matters, fairly disclosed with enough detail for the Buyer to identify their nature and scope, and stated against specific warranties. No disclosure should qualify title, capacity, tax, the fundamental warranties or any specific indemnity.
- DL 1.4 (no admission) is broadly acceptable. However, it must not dilute the factual content of the specific disclosures, and it must not suggest that a consent, payment or release is not required where the SPA makes it a condition.

**8. Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3).**
- The bar covers the Buyer **or its advisers**, and anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge at its widest.
- Combined with item 7, it would neutralise claims on every matter the Seller has disclosed, including matters we are negotiating specific protection for.
- **Push-back:** delete. If a knowledge qualifier must appear anywhere, it should run the other way: Seller knowledge limited to named individuals, after reasonable enquiry. It should never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity. Also add an express statement that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge.

### C. Specific transaction matters

**9. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3).**
- Bluefen is roughly AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, about 30% of the business. That makes it a material customer by any measure.
- The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied "on delivery" of a written consent. DL 2 confirms that, as at 22 September, there was no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions were satisfied.
- Consent-on-delivery could be met by a consent that is conditional, revocable or subject to unmet cl 11.3 conditions.
- **Push-back:**
  - Make this a condition precedent to Completion requiring an effective, unconditional (or Buyer-approved) written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2.
  - Require evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that every cl 11.3 condition is satisfied before Completion.
  - Upgrade the obligation from reasonable endeavours to best or all reasonable endeavours, with Buyer review of the consent request.
  - Add a waiver right for the Buyer only, a sunset date, and a termination right.
  - Ask for current status now.

**10. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7).**
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, roughly 13% of the price. DL 3 confirms it had not been repaid and there was no discharge. The Seller offers only a release "following Completion".
- Under a debt-free deal, that would leave the Company encumbered at Completion, with the Buyer relying on an unsecured promise. Change-control cl 8.1 may also be triggered by Completion itself.
- **Push-back:**
  - Require a current payout letter (the figure is described only as "approximately").
  - Repayment should be made directly to Riverlark from Completion funds and treated as Debt in the price mechanics.
  - Executed deeds of release and security discharges (including PPSR releases and any other registrations) should be delivered at Completion.
  - A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists, so our position is release at Completion.

**11. Employee bonuses and the funds flow.**
- The cover note says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics". DL 5 admits that the AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are not in it, and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- These bonuses are triggered by Completion. "A matter for the Seller" has no contractual effect: unless the bonuses are itemised or Seller-funded, the cost lands on the Company, and therefore on us.
- **Push-back:**
  - Add a specific line item, treated as Debt or Transaction Expenses, deducted from the price or paid by the Seller.
  - Cover the AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs (payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding administration, any other employer costs), quantified before Completion.
  - Back this with a specific indemnity.
  - Obtain the bonus letters and confirm the conditions.

**12. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1).**
- The indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee.
- The risk is therefore wider than one payment. It covers failure of title to the materials, Ironquay infringement or ownership claims, and the cost of remediation or re-development.
- The AUD 180,000 shown as open in DD-010 is not independently verified. We should not treat it as confirmed unpaid, and we should not accept that the matter is minor either.
- **Push-back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of SOW3 Project Materials and related IP to vest in the Company, and from any Ironquay claim. Place it outside the general cap, basket and time limits.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees, Ironquay's confirmation of receipt, and a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a Completion deliverable.
  - Request bank evidence and Ironquay's written statement of account.

**13. DD-006 export incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6).**
- The Seller calls the incident "not expected to be material". That is an assertion. Its own DL 6 says the investigation is preliminary, and that access, scope and any notification requirement are not established. About 1,240 records with personal information may be involved.
- Consistent with the playbook, we should **not** assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure. Equally, we should not accept the "immaterial" characterisation.
- **Push-back:**
  - Add pre-Completion covenants:
    - preserve all logs and evidence;
    - continue and complete a proper investigation, including the assessment of whether notification is required;
    - give the Buyer regular written updates and access;
    - take no regulator or affected-person communications without Buyer consultation, subject to legal requirements.
  - Add a bring-down of the position at Completion.
  - Keep any specific protection scoped to whatever the investigation reveals, without a pre-set number.

**14. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).**
- The Seller labels these "ordinary-course operating costs". DL 8 says the material does not establish whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. It also notes the three AUD 110k renewals are related and should be read together.
- Splitting related items into three may matter for thresholds or approval limits. That is a reason to look closer, not a conclusion.
- **Push-back:** do not accept the ordinary-course label, and do not automatically treat the amounts as Debt or a price deduction. Obtain the DD-008 and DD-011 contracts and assess timing, terminability, accrual and business rationale. Then decide whether a specific warranty, conduct-of-business consent right or adjustment is warranted.

**15. Tax and IP.**
- The Seller says these positions are "settled under the general regime". Our playbook records them as **OPEN**.
- **Push-back:** reject the characterisation, keep the Tax and IP categories separate from the general regime, and leave the terms open for negotiation. We should not assume either unlimited liability or a resolution.

**16. Title (DD-012).**
- The share register is a Seller-supplied internal document. The Seller's own DL 10 concedes it is a source relied on, not Buyer verification.
- **Push-back:** require independent evidence:
  - a current ASIC company extract and the history of share issues and transfers;
  - share certificates;
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, and encumbrance confirmations;
  - the constitution and any shareholder agreement (checking pre-emption and transfer restrictions);
  - the Seller's corporate authority (board resolutions).

  Title and capacity warranties should sit in the fundamental regime (item 5).

**17. Lower-order items: DD-007 lease and DD-009 Mossvale.**
- The Seller states that only a landlord notification is needed, and that Mossvale's assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. These readings may well be right, but we should confirm them from the documents ourselves rather than rely on the Disclosure Letter.
- Make the lease notification a Completion deliverable or covenant.

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Non-negotiable (no authority exists to concede):**
1. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 / 12–13).
2. Title and capacity in a separate fundamental regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
3. Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" default (cl 13), and keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate.

**Restate playbook positions:**
4. Cap at 25% / AUD 6m. Do **not** offer 20%: it needs Amelia Frost's written authority, which has not been given, and the matching figure does not clear it.
5. De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k on a first-dollar basis.
6. Claims period of 24 months (18 months is unauthorised).
7. Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2) and require specific fair disclosure only.
8. Delete the buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3).

**Transaction-specific protections:**
9. Bluefen: CP requiring effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, a stronger endeavours obligation, a Buyer-only waiver, and termination rights.
10. Riverlark: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases and discharges delivered at Completion.
11. Bonuses: AUD 420k plus all on-costs as an itemised funds-flow line or Seller-funded, backed by an indemnity.
12. Ironquay: broadened indemnity outside the general regime, with the SOW3 cure preserved and the AUD 180k verified independently.
13. DD-006: preservation, investigation, update and consultation covenants, with no assumed breach or figure in either direction.
14. Sandbar: diligence first, with no ordinary-course concession and no automatic Debt or deduction.
15. Tax and IP: record them as open and reject "settled".
16. Title: independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence beyond DD-012.

**Process:**
17. In the cover note, state clearly that we do not accept the draft as "final", "agreed", "pre-cleared" or "market", and that all positions remain open.
18. Request a refreshed Disclosure Letter and status update dated close to signing. Any new disclosure between signing and Completion should not cure warranty breaches without Buyer rights to claim or terminate.
19. Before any fallback is used, escalate internally to Amelia Frost for written authority identifying this specific draft. Given how far off-side this draft is, I would not recommend seeking that authority yet.

I can turn this into a mark-up issues list or a draft response to Seller's counsel if helpful.
